page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and hyper-threading running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, and 125 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. Standard CPU and memory operations, such as stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark tests, consistently rank in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, database and web serving benchmarks show weak throughput. However, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance for specialized workloads. LLM inference benchmarks for small 135M and medium 7B models show top-tier prompt processing speeds and strong text generation rates, though larger models like the 70B variant are not supported due to memory constraints.

The g4dn.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency by bundling a dedicated GPU and local NVMe storage within a lower-tier resource profile, avoiding the higher costs associated with larger multi-GPU instances. This makes it suitable for entry-level machine learning inference, small-scale LLM deployment, graphics-intensive applications, and lightweight GPU-accelerated development tasks, while general-purpose compute tasks are better served by non-GPU instances.
